record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.context_brief: limits of the Principle of Indifference
record.original_question: For nonequilibrium phenomena such as anomalous Levy-like diffusion, fractal motion, and self-organized criticality where ordinary Fick or Fourier diffusion equations may fail, when does the Shannon-Jaynes Principle of Indifference cease to apply, and what generalized entropy or cross-entropy measure should replace the usual MaxEnt or Kullback-Leibler construction?

evidence.quote: At this point, it can be rised the question of the possibility of situations when the Principle of Indifference may be seen as not applying.

This seems to be the case of some phenomena said to follow Levy's distributions. In condensed matter, Fick (or Fourier) diffusion equations are, for certain systems, nonvalid and a so-called anomalous Levy-like diffusion is present.
But some problems can require non-exponential distributions, such that additivity - or better to say Euler homogeneity of order one - in the statistical functions is not satisfied.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns when Shannon–Jaynes MaxEnt fails for anomalous-diffusion/Lévy/self-organized-criticality systems and what generalized entropy should replace it. Multiple candidate generalizations exist in the literature (Tsallis q-entropy, Rényi entropy, Kaniadakis κ-entropy, superstatistics, group entropies of Tempesta), each successful in specific regimes, but no consensus exists on a single replacement nor on a sharp criterion delimiting the failure of the Principle of Indifference. The problem is generally regarded as open and active.

status_evidence.title: Nonadditive entropy and nonextensive statistical mechanics - Tsallis
status_evidence.snippet: Ongoing research on q-entropy and generalizations for anomalous-diffusion and long-range systems.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing generalized entropies (Tsallis, Rényi, Kaniadakis, group entropies) are still being proposed and debated.

status_evidence.title: Group entropies, information geometry and rigorous foundations (Tempesta)
status_evidence.snippet: A general axiomatic framework for admissible generalized entropies is developed, indicating no unique replacement is established.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of which entropy is appropriate in which physical regime remains an open program.
